Graz takes off his junk helmet
and thumbs out a dent.
감자만 들어간다고 하셨죠.\n장터 애들한테 그대로 말했어요.\n…아무도:
You said only potatoes go in.
I told the market lot just that.
…Nobody believes me. Hmph.
'넣을 거면 벌써 넣었지.'\n그 말, 사흘 동안 생각했어요.\n…맞는:
'If I meant to, I'd have done it.'
I chewed on that for three days.
…Scarier, 'cause it's true.
실은요, 우리 무리는 새 굴에\n제일 작은 놈을 먼저 보내요.\n살아 나:
Truth is, our band sends
the smallest one into a new den.
If he comes out, the rest follow.
이 집엔 제가 먼저 온 거예요.\n…자원했어요! 진짜로!\n제비뽑기에서:
So I came to this house first.
…I volunteered! Truly!
I didn't lose the drawing of lots.
제일 작은 자가 먼저 갑니다.\n요정의 숲에서도 그렇지요.\n…고블린도:
The smallest goes first.
So it is in the fairy wood, too.
…I did not know goblins did so.
요, 요정 나리랑 같은 편은\n처음이에요. 기분 이상하네…\n좋은 쪽으로:
M-me on the same side as
a fairy lord… Feels strange…
The good kind of strange.
I never even asked
about drawing lots.
정말요? 다 오면 열둘인데요?\n…아, 한꺼번엔 안 와요!\n셋씩. 셋씩:
Really? That's twelve of us!
…Oh, not all at once!
Threes. In threes, see.
고블린은 방값을 나눠 내요.\n열둘이 나누면 한 명당…\n…피클한테 물어:
Goblins split the room fee.
Twelve ways, that makes each…
…I'll ask Pikl.
What I saw?
The soup's good, the Witch is scary,
and the sheep are gentle.
…Can I leave out the scary bit?
No? All right.
Today I'll sit in the middle,
not by the door.
…Just half a seat further in.
Graz's junk armor bears
three fresh claw marks.
사촌 셋이 왔다 갔어요.\n저더러 '마녀 집 용사'래요.\n…밤엔 셋 다:
Three cousins came and went.
They call me 'the Witch's hero.'
…At night all three hid in bed.
본 대로 말했어요. 무섭다고.\n다들 웃었는데 할머니가\n'그래도 갔구나:
I told them what I saw. Scary.
They all laughed, but Granny said,
'Still, you went.'
어젯밤 괴물 왔을 때요.\n저, 안 도망쳤어요.\n문 앞에 끝까지 서 있:
When the monster came last night,
I didn't run.
I stood at the door to the end.
…처음부터 끝까지 무서웠어요.\n다리가 계속 떨렸어요.\n그건 비밀이에요:
…I was scared start to finish.
My legs kept shaking.
That part's a secret.
다리 떨린 건 나도 봤소.\n그래도 안 물러섰지.\n…문 옆 자리, 반:
I saw your legs shake too.
Yet you never stepped back.
…I'll share my spot by the door.
H-half? Your spot, big brother?
…Then not the sword side.
The wall-side half.
The armor may be junk,
but where he stood was not.
하! 그럼요! 원래 용감했…\n…아니에요. 오늘 처음이에요.\n오늘 처음:
Ha! Of course! Always was brav…
…No. Today's the first time.
First time I was ever brave.
Sleep in the inner room next time.
…안쪽 방이요.\n걱정해 주시는 거죠?\n쫓아내는 거 아니죠?:
…The inner room.
You're worried for me, right?
Not throwing me out, right?
그래도 문 앞에 설래요.\n안쪽 방은 다리 떨릴 때\n도망칠 자리로 맡아:
I'll still stand at the door.
The inner room I'll keep as
my place to flee when legs shake.
Next time I won't run.
…Really, this time.
Strategically or otherwise.
원래 있었다고 했지.\n밤마다 다시 셌소. 여덟.\n…이젠 여덟이 맞는:
You said it was there all along.
Recounted every night. Eight.
…Eight seems right now.
You said not to count.
Held off three days. On the fourth,
there was one more trap.
The black sheep is eighth again.
…Always the last one in.
숲에 덫을 일곱 놨는데\n여덟이 됐다고 했지.\n그 여덟째, 누구 건지:
Seven traps I set in the forest,
and they became eight, I said.
I know whose the eighth is now.
Pikl draws out a knotted cord.
At its end, an unfamiliar knot.
이 매듭, 우리 집 매듭이오.\n세 번 감고 한 번 뒤집는 거.\n…형이:
This knot is our family's knot.
Three wraps, one flip.
…The way my brother tied them.
…I saw that trap too.
At night. A goblin
left it. Quietly.
봤다고? 몇 시에? 몇 걸음?\n…아니, 됐소. 삵한테\n걸음 수까지 묻:
Saw it? What hour? How many steps?
…No, never mind. I'll not ask
a wildcat to count paces.
Three wraps, one flip.
…The counting hand trembles.
Leave that trap as it is.
…As it is. Yes.
Touch it and he'd know
that I'd come.
Then I'll only count it, mornings.
Seven, and one.
Tie one more knot onto it.
…답장이라.\n고블린은 글 대신 매듭이오.\n'나 여기 있소' 한 번 감:
…A reply, then.
Goblins write in knots.
'I am here' is one wrap.
Will he read it?
…He taught it to me, after all.
Tonight, not traps. I'll count
my brother's years instead.
…Twenty-nine. No, thirty.
매듭이 하나 더 묶여 있었소.\n'나 여기 있소'에\n'안다' 한 번 감:
Another knot had been tied.
To 'I am here,'
one wrap: 'I know.'
덫이 사라졌소. 그 자리에\n토끼 한 마리가 있더군.\n…형이 셈을 맞춰:
The trap was gone. In its place
sat a rabbit.
…He squared the count and left.
You never asked me
why I count so.
…I'll tell you.
흉년 겨울에 형이 곳간을 셌소.\n하나를 틀렸지.\n그 겨울, 우리 넷이:
One lean winter he counted stores.
He got one wrong.
That winter, the four of us starved.
In spring he left the den.
Blamed his own count.
…Since then I count. His share too.
그 매듭 표식, 북쪽 고개에서\n본 적 있어요. 바위마다요.\n길잡이 눈:
That knot mark, I've seen it
on the north pass. Every rock.
A guide's eye catches it all.
…The north pass. Half a day off.
Thank you, fox.
One wrong count,
and two brothers counting for life.
I'll keep a room free for him.
Then this house has one less
empty room. …No.
One count comes out right.
You can put the counting down.
못 하오. 하지만\n오늘 밤 하나는 안 세겠소.\n당신 창문. 그건 안:
I can't. But
tonight there's one I won't count.
Your windows. Those I won't count.
형이 오면 같이 세 봅시다.\n양 일곱, 검은 양 하나.\n…틀려도 되는:
When he comes, we'll count together.
Seven sheep, one black sheep.
…A count allowed to be wrong.
Heh heh, for real this time.
셋째 톱의 출처: Where the Third Saw Came From
Didn't look at the staff! Honest!
…Only twice.
In passing.
톱이 좋냐고 물어봤지?\n그 뒤로 톱 얘기 할 데가\n생겨서 좋았어. 헤:
You asked if I liked saws, yeah?
After that I had someone
to talk saws with. Heh heh.
Rusk lays three saws on the table
in order of size.
첫째는 산 거, 둘째는\n내기에서 딴 거. 셋째는…\n묻지 말랬지? 오늘:
First one I bought, second I won
on a bet. The third…
You said don't ask? Today I'll tell.
고물 더미에서 주웠어.\n날이 휘었다고 버린 거야.\n근데 휜 게 아니라:
Picked it off a junk heap.
Tossed out 'cause the blade bent.
But it's not bent. It's smiling.
…That saw.
Those are my hammer marks.
Heh, heh heh… said not to ask.
…I threw it out. Blade was bent.
…You use it well.
I'll set the teeth again myself.
Three saws laid end to end
still fall short of his bragging.
If you found it, it's yours.
Right? Right?
A junk heap is a goblin market.
Whoever tossed it is a customer.
…But sometimes I feel bad.
For whoever threw away
something that cuts this well.
Just tell me the saws' names.
Names! First is 'Clanger,'
second is 'Gutsy,'
third… 'Grinner.'
날이 휘어서 웃는 것 같거든.\n버려진 걸 고블린이 주우면\n다 웃게 돼:
The bent blade looks like a grin.
When a goblin picks up a castoff,
it always ends up grinning.
A saw doesn't lie.
If it cuts well, it cuts well.
…Even if it was thrown out.
By the door, a stool I've never seen.
Wood shavings still cling to it.
웃음이로 켰어. 셋째 톱.\n주운 톱으로 만든 걸상이야.\n나무는 바람에:
Cut it with Grinner. Third saw.
A stool made with a found saw.
The wood blew down in a gale!
깡깡이로 자르고 배짱이로 켜고\n웃음이로 다듬었어.\n셋 다 힘을 보탰어:
Cut with Clanger, ripped with Gutsy,
smoothed with Grinner.
All three pitched in.
고블린 물건은 이틀이면\n무너진다고들 하잖아.\n…다들 그래. 고블린 식:
They say goblin things fall apart
in two days.
…Everyone says it. 'Goblin-made.'
이건 이틀 넘게 서 있을 거야.\n한 달. 아니, 한 겨울.\n…서 있었:
This one'll stand past two days.
A month. No, a whole winter.
…I hope it stands.
…쐐기를 박았군. 하나.\n고블린치곤…:
…Drove in a wedge. Just one.
For a goblin…
How many times has he heard
'goblin-made,' I wonder.
The stool creaks once,
then falls quiet.
The creak was a hello! A hello!
…It held. It held!
Heh heh, heh heh heh.
If it creaks, make it again.
Yes! 'Again' is a good word.
Nobody ever told a goblin
'do it again.' Just 'toss it.'
내일은 걸상 다리부터 셀 거야.\n사흘째에도 서 있으면\n그날을 내 생일:
Tomorrow I start by counting legs.
If it's still standing on day three,
that'll be my birthday.
약속은 주머니에 안 들어간다고\n했잖아요. 그래서 만들었어요.\n약속 주:
You said promises don't fit
in pockets. So I made one.
A promise pouch!
두 배 무서워서 안 만졌어요.\n진짜예요. 대신 오래 봤어요.\n보는 건:
Twice as scary, so I didn't touch.
Honest. I looked a long time instead.
Looking's free, right?
Tak opens the new pouch.
Inside are three pebbles.
약속 하나에 조약돌 하나요.\n'등불 안 만짐' 하나,\n'단추 안 가져:
One pebble for each promise.
One for 'didn't touch the lamp,'
one for 'didn't take buttons'…
The third is a secret.
…It's got to do with
something I found on the roof.
지붕에서? 혹시 솔잎 화살?\n끝에 빨간 실 묶인 거?\n그거 내 거야!:
On the roof? A pine-needle arrow?
With a red thread tied at the end?
That's mine!
주, 주운 거예요!\n모자 옆에 굴러 있었어요.\n…돌려드릴게요. 셋째:
I-I found it!
It was rolling by a hat.
…I'll give it back. Third promise.
Each time a pouch was added,
this house's things did not dwindle.
…Not yet.
Put a promise of mine in too.
진짜요? 마녀님 약속이요?\n뭐로 할까요… 뭐로 하지…:
Really? A promise from you, Witch?
What'll it be… what, what…
'다음 겨울에도 문 열어 줌.'\n…이걸로 할게요!\n제일 큰 조약돌로요:
'Door opens again next winter.'
…That one!
With the biggest pebble.
Give what you found to its owners.
…알았어요. 대신 주인을\n못 찾은 건 어떡해요?\n그건 제가 맡아 둬도:
…All right. But what about
things whose owners I can't find?
Can I hold on to those?
오늘 밤엔 조약돌을 세 번 셀래요.\n피클 아저씨처럼요.\n…세 번까지만:
Tonight I'll count my pebbles thrice.
Like Mister Pikl.
…Only up to three times.
제일 큰 조약돌 아직 있어요.\n'다음 겨울에도 문 열어 줌.'\n…매일:
The biggest pebble's still here.
'Door opens again next winter.'
…I touch it every day.
돌려줄 수 있는 건 다 줬어요.\n남은 건 주인 없는 것들이에요.\n…이:
I gave back all I could.
What's left has no owners.
…These weigh the most.
Tak turns out each pouch in turn.
Buttons, glass beads, a rusty key.
할머니가 그랬어요.\n반짝이는 건 누가 잃어버린 거래요.\n줍는 건 기억:
Granny said so.
Shiny things are things someone lost.
Picking them up is remembering.
그래서 주워요. 잃어버린 사람을\n저라도 기억하려고요.\n…다들 그냥 도:
So I pick them up. So someone
remembers the ones who lost them.
…Everyone just calls me a thief.
이건 이 집 울타리 밑에서\n주웠어요. 늘 차가워요.\n…드릴게요. 원래:
I found this under your fence.
It's always cold.
…Here. It belongs here anyway.
A glass orb the size of a palm,
frost patterns frozen inside.
A ward orb that hung on the fence.
I never knew it was lost.
Keep it. Remember it for me.
…그럼 제일 깊은 주머니에\n넣을게요. 할머니 단추 옆에요.\n거기가 제:
…Then it goes in my deepest pouch.
Next to Granny's button.
That's the safest place.
Thank you. I'll hang it again.
고맙다고 하셨어요!\n고블린한테요! 주운 걸로요!:
You said thank you!
To a goblin! For something found!
…My pouch is light
but my heart is heavy.
Heavy the good way.
Only good things in the new pouch.
…Not just things I found.
Things I was given, too.
'수프가 됨'으로 선전했어요.\n공짜로요. 그랬더니\n배고픈 손님만 몰려:
I advertised 'Becomes Soup.'
For free. And then
only hungry customers came.
'안 잡아먹음' 뺐어요.\n대신 '잡아먹음 없음(대체로)'.\n…손님이:
I dropped 'Won't Eat You.'
Now it's 'No Eating (Mostly).'
…Customers halved.
그건 그렇고! 제안 하나.\n이 산장 좌판 독점 계약.\n저만 팔고, 저:
Anyway! A proposal.
Sole trading rights at this lodge.
Only I sell, only I buy.
That badger every third day?
That furball snatches all
my regulars. Honest prices, too!
Is honesty a flaw now?
Goblin, I walked this
forest road first.
먼저요? 우리 할머니가\n이 길에서 단추를 팔 때\n오소리는 굴에서 자고:
First? When my granny sold
buttons on this road,
badgers were asleep in their setts!
…One of those buttons is still
on my stall.
At an honest price.
Two stalls in my yard,
squabbling over my guests.
No monopoly. Both of you come.
Both? Aw…
Then I'll dodge the badger's day
and come on the second.
…사흘 중 이틀은 제 거예요.\n셈은 제가 이겼죠?:
…Two days in three are mine.
I won the count, right?
Cheaper? Telling a goblin
to sell cheaper is telling him
to breathe only halfway.
…Fine. A button free with each.
That badger
can't match that.
숙박비는 제값. 흥정 없이.\n…오늘도요. 이상하네,\n이 집에선 흥정이:
Lodging at full price. No haggling.
…Again today. Odd,
haggling never works in this house.
첫 동전 대신: In Place of the First Coin
그 오소리랑 하루 걸러\n오다 보니… 정이 들었어요.\n말은 하지 마세요:
Coming every other day with
that badger… I've grown fond.
Don't tell anyone.
단추 덤 덕에 손님이 늘었어요.\n단추가 다 떨어졌죠.\n…이제 제 소매:
The free buttons drew customers.
Ran clean out of buttons.
…Now it's my sleeve buttons.
고블린 장사꾼은 처음 번 동전을\n평생 안 써요. 목에 걸죠.\n…그걸:
A goblin trader never spends
his first coin. Wears it on his neck.
…I lost mine in the forest.
But in its place
there was this.
Nib unfolds a yellowed paper.
A torn corner of a ledger.
제 이름이 적혀 있어요.\n엄청 오래된 글씨로요.\n거래를 한 것 같다는:
My name's written on it.
In very old handwriting.
That's why I think I made a deal.
I know this hand.
A ledger that smells of
candles at dusk.
니브. 그건 값 못 매겨요.\n그거 팔면 내가 평생\n당신 좌판 안 봐요:
Nib. That can't be priced.
Sell it, and I'll never look
at your stall again.
…Even Mala can't price it, she says.
So it must be truly dear.
Don't sell it. It's a charm.
부적이요? 이게 지켜 준다고요?\n…동전이 하던 일을\n종이가 하는 거네:
A charm? This'll protect me?
…So the paper does
what the coin used to.
I'll wear it where the coin hung.
…It's light. Strangely.
얼마에 팔 건데?: How much would you sell it for?
…It's not for sale.
First time ever. Not naming a price.
…Surprised myself.
다음 선전 문구 정했어요.\n'마녀의 산장, 안 잡아먹음.\n잃은 건 다:
Got my next slogan.
'The Witch's Lodge: Won't Eat You.
Lost things return as other things.'
곰일 거라 하셨죠?\n다시 가 봤어요. 곰이었어요!\n…곰이 돌 침대에서:
You said it'd be a bear, right?
Went back. A bear it was!
…Sleeping on a stone bed.
You asked what it said, right?
So I went to ask.
…Nobody there. Only tracks.
근데 그 동굴 벽에 그림이 있어요.\n등불 든 사람들이요.\n…이 몸 그:
But the cave wall has paintings.
People holding lanterns.
…Yours truly, Grik, gulped.
으음… 그 동굴, 숲 안쪽?\n우리 큰아버지 겨울잠 자리일걸.\n돌 침대:
Mmm… that cave, deep in the wood?
Probably my uncle's winter bed.
He was fond of stone beds.
A mural of lantern-bearers,
guarded now by a bear.
Not bad.
'Bear Here'… no flair.
…Fine. But big letters.
'Bear Here. Very Big.'
역시! 마녀님은 탐험가 편이에요!: Knew it! You're an explorer's friend!
…But writing it that way,
the pen feels heavy.
I'll write half. 'Warlock (bear).'
백 개의 동굴까지 하나 남았어요.\n…아니, 둘. 아니, 사실은…\n…다:
One more to a hundred caves.
…No, two. No, honestly…
…I'll tell you next time.
I wrote 'Bear Here,'
and the map sold at market.
First time ever.
I wrote 'Warlock (bear),'
and everyone laughed.
…Because of the brackets.
백 개의 동굴, 사실은 열한 개예요.\n열하나도 많은 거예요!\n…근데:
A hundred caves? It's eleven, truly.
Eleven's a lot too!
…But nobody will listen.
고블린 탐험가는 열을 말해야\n하나를 믿어 줘요.\n그래서 열 배로 말해:
A goblin explorer must say ten
to be believed for one.
So I say it tenfold.
Grik spreads a torn map.
In one corner is this lodge.
축척은 엉망인데\n길은 맞소. 바위 하나까지.\n…고블린 지도는 처음 보:
The scale is a shambles,
but the roads are true. To the rock.
…My first goblin map.
…Roads are true, he says! A scholar!
This I won't tell tenfold.
열한 개를 백 개로 말해야\n듣는 사람이 생긴다.\n…세상이 그렇게 만들:
Call eleven a hundred,
and someone finally listens.
…The world made it so.
…열한 개요. 그쵸?\n열하나도 대단하죠?:
…Eleven. Right?
Eleven's grand too, isn't it?
Then this house is the twelfth.
Not a cave, mind.
…A warm cave.
Say a hundred. I'll back you.
You'd back me up, Witch?
…Then you'd be
a liar too.
…안 돼요. 그건 안 돼요.\n열한 개라고 할게요.\n마녀님 말은 비싸니:
…No. That won't do.
I'll say eleven.
Your word costs too much, Witch.
지도에 이 집은 그려져요.\n열 배로 안 부풀려도\n…원래 큰 집이니까요:
This house goes on the map.
No tenfold puffing needed.
…It's a big house already.
Mala polishes her monocle.
The third time already.
워록의 얼굴일지도 모른다고\n하셨죠. 그 뒤로 동전이\n…더 웃는 것 같:
You said it might be a warlock's
face. Since then the coin
…seems to smile more.
동전은 안 팔았어요. 원칙이니까.\n근데 그 뒤로\n등불이 자꾸 생각나요:
I didn't sell the coin. Principle.
But ever since,
I keep thinking of the lantern.
등불 바닥에 장인 표식이 있어요.\n눈송이 하나, 줄 넷.\n…어느 장부:
There's a maker's mark on its base.
One snowflake, four lines.
…A mark in no ledger I know.
So I'll ask properly.
That lantern. Name your price.
말라 씨가 값을 부르라면\n조심하세요. 그 말 뒤에\n장터 하나가 사라졌:
If Mala says name your price,
take care. After those words,
they say a whole market vanished.
You exaggerate, Sera.
…It was half a market.
Even Grandmother's grandmother
never knew this lantern's price.
I know. I asked
to hear you say it.
안 파는 물건이 있는 집이\n진짜 부자인 집이거든요.\n…이 집, 부자네:
A house with things it won't sell
is a truly rich house.
…This house is rich.
…My whole collection.
Enough to fill three goblin dens.
Half a jest.
…The other half's earnest,
and that scares me too.
등불은 꼭 제게 파세요.\n…아니, 팔지 마세요.\n제가 그냥 보러 올게:
Sell the lantern to me, no one else.
…No, don't sell it.
I'll just come and look.
안경을 벗어도 될까요?: May I take off my monocle?
안 파는 물건이 있는 집.\n…그 말, 할머니 말이에요.\n제가 지어낸:
A house with things it won't sell.
…Those were Granny's words.
I didn't make them up.
수집품 전부라고 했던 거,\n굴에 가서 다시 셌어요.\n…등불 하나만 못:
My whole collection, I said.
Went home and counted again.
…Not worth that one lantern.
이 외알 안경, 할머니 거예요.\n감정사 집안의 물건이죠.\n할머니가 그:
This monocle was my granny's.
An heirloom of appraisers.
Granny used to say,
'값을 못 매기는 걸 만나면\n안경을 벗어라.\n그건 눈으로 보는 게 아:
'When you meet what can't be priced,
take off the glass.
That's not seen with the eye.'
Mala removes her monocle, a first.
A round mark rings her eye.
Child, a granny's gifts
are meant to be used.
Knowing to remove it is using it.
…Grannies all say the same thing.
Whatever the race.
Bare eyes look on the hearth.
A face that names no price.
But even blurry, the fire
is warm. I see it not by price
but by warmth.
A house that opens its door
every night for that price.
…That's why I can't price it.
Next time I'll come without it.
…And I'll only appraise
at the door.
Graz the hero is here!
…Legs still shaking today.
But I came.
Inner room's empty, right?
…Won't use it. Just checking.
Cousins send their regards!
They'll come in threes, threes.
One room still empty?
…Counted. Still empty.
Good.
Didn't count the windows today.
…There are four, though.
One more knot now.
My brother's. I counted.
Stool still standing?
…It is! Heh heh.
What day is it now?
Whittled new stool legs!
This one won't creak. Probably.
Clanger, Gutsy, Grinner.
All three say hello.
The orb's still cold!
It's in my deepest pouch.
I saw the fence orb!
…Didn't touch it. Just looked.
조약돌 가져왔어요.\n'다음 겨울에도 문 열어 줌.'\n…지금 겨울이에요:
Brought the pebble.
'Door opens again next winter.'
…It's winter now!
Want to see what's round my neck?
…No price on it. Not this one.
Fancy a bit of haggling?
…Anything but what's on my neck.
Not the badger's day, is it?
…Counted right. Day two.
Made it to the twelfth cave!
…The warm one.
No puffing it up today.
…Only a little puffing.
That cave bear's still asleep.
I tiptoed here.
Monocle's in my pocket.
…Today I'll see things blurry.
One night's room, here.
…The very price I named.
Lantern still here?
…Not buying. Just came to look.
